title: Unveiling the Spin-Valley Structure of Dipolar Exciton Ladders in R-stacked WSe$_2$/WS$_2$ Moiré Heterobilayers
authors: Byeong Wook Cho, Tatyana V. Ivanova, Zhe Li, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Brian D. Gerardot, Mauro Brotons-Gisbert
abstract: Localized interlayer excitons in moiré heterobilayers can form dipolar exciton ladders, yet their internal spin-valley structure remains unresolved. Here, we use helicity-resolved magneto-photoluminescence to identify the microscopic origin of the ladder in R-stacked WSe$_2$/WS$_2$ at charge neutrality and one-electron filling of the moiré lattice. At charge neutrality, the first two emission peaks correspond to a spin-triplet interlayer exciton and a triplet-triplet two-exciton state separated by 38 meV, reflecting the on-site dipolar interaction. The opposite Zeeman response of the apparent third rung of the ladder rules out its assignment as a spin-conserving three-exciton state and instead identifies it as a triplet-singlet two-exciton configuration with a 22 meV offset set by the WS$_2$ conduction-band spin splitting. At one-electron filling, the correlated electronic background gives rise to charged one- and two-exciton states and intervalley/intravalley two-exciton configurations, while reducing the effective exciton-exciton interaction. Our results establish a spin-valley-resolved picture of dipolar exciton ladders beyond simple occupation-number physics in moiré heterobilayers.
summary: The authors used helicity-resolved magnetophotoluminescence on WSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayers to map the internal structure of dipolar exciton ladders. They successfully assigned the ladder's components ($	ext{IX}1, 	ext{IX}2, 	ext{IX}3$) by analyzing their spin and valley polarization responses under magnetic fields. The results provide a fundamental understanding of how excitonic interactions are governed by both geometry (R-stacking) and external doping.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the internal spin-valley structure of dipolar exciton ladders formed by localized interlayer excitons in R-stacked WSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayers.
main_result: They established a detailed spin-valley picture, identifying the ladder components as $	ext{IX1}(	ext{T}) ightarrow 	ext{IX2}(	ext{T},	ext{T}) ightarrow 	ext{IX3}(	ext{T},	ext{S})$, and showed that resident carriers significantly modify this structure.
method: Helicity-resolved magneto-photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy was used, combined with analysis of Zeeman splitting and circular polarization ($ho$) as a function of magnetic field and carrier density.
model_or_system: The system is R-stacked WSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayers hosting localized interlayer excitons (IXs). The physics involves dipolar interactions ($U_{dd}$) and spin-valley coupling, which are probed by measuring the energy and polarization of emitted photons.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on optical selection rules linking valley transitions to specific polarizations, and fitting Zeeman splittings to determine effective exciton g-factors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate PL spectra showing the emergence of discrete ladder peaks ($	ext{IX}2$ at $38 	ext{ meV}$ above $	ext{IX}1$), magnetic field dependence used for Zeeman splitting, and filling-dependent spectral evolution across different doping regimes.
paper_structure:
The paper systematically analyzes the exciton ladder structure first at charge neutrality ($
u=0$) using magneto-PL to assign spin/valley states. It then investigates the effect of electron doping ($
u=1$), observing changes in interaction strength, and finally examines hole doping ($
u=-1$) to map out the full phase diagram.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly detailed spectroscopic fingerprint of interacting excitons in 2D van der Waals heterostructures, directly mapping spin and valley degrees of freedom using magneto-optics—a key area for quantum simulation platforms.
